correctness.rationale: With Euclidean mirror maps and \(e^{a_t}=\dot b_t\), the source first-order equations transform exactly under \(s=e^{b_t}\) to \(x_s=(z_x-x)/s\), \((z_x)_s=-(\mu x+z_\lambda)\), and \((z_\lambda)_s=z_x\). Differentiation gives the invariant \(I=sx-z_\lambda\) and the exact scalar equation \(w_{ss}+(1+\mu/s)w=I\) for \(w=sx\). Shifting by the instantaneous equilibrium reduces the forcing to an integrable \((s+\mu)^{-3}\) term, and the displayed energy inequality gives a uniform bound on \(w\). On \(I=0\), the oscillator energy has a strictly positive lower bound for every nonzero solution, which prevents \(w\to0\) and proves exponent sharpness.

value.rationale: The scalar equality constraint is the canonical feasibility mode of an affine primal--dual flow, and the source theorem explicitly distinguishes squared-feasibility from the stronger residual rate. The hidden invariant explains when that gap disappears without friction, gives an exact one-dimensional reduction, and proves that the resulting \(e^{-b_t}\) exponent is itself sharp. This identifies a concrete acceleration mechanism--position/lookahead cancellation rather than damping--that is useful for interpreting the new variational flow and for testing which parts of the generic Lyapunov assumptions are structural versus conservative.
